How Much Does Pool Service Cost in Phoenix?

Published price ranges for recurring pool service, one-time cleanups and common repairs, what pushes a Phoenix price up or down, and how to compare written quotes. The line sets no prices; every figure here comes from a named source.

Call (623) 240-0428 Jump to the price factors
  1. Home
  2. Pool Service Cost

How much does pool service cost in Phoenix? There is no single number, and anyone who quotes one over the phone without seeing the pool is guessing. The price depends on the size of the pool, how often it is visited, who supplies the chemicals, how much falls into the water and the age of the equipment. This guide pulls together published 2026 ranges for recurring service, one-time cleanups and common repairs, explains what moves a Phoenix price up or down, and shows how to compare quotes fairly.

A word on where these numbers come from. Phoenix Pool Cleaning Pro is a free phone line, not a pool company, and it never prices a job. A call is handed to an independent, locally owned pool service company in the Valley, and that company inspects the pool and sets its own price. Each dollar figure on this page is credited to the cost guide that published it, with links at the end. Treat them as background reading: actual quotes for Phoenix pools vary.

Pool service cost: published ranges

Angi and HomeGuide both publish 2026 pricing for pool care, gathered from what homeowners and contractors report. Their figures differ, and that is normal; the overlap between them is the most useful part. Some rows below are specific to Phoenix and some are national, as marked.

Published pool service and cleaning cost ranges from Angi and HomeGuide, 2026
What you are paying forPublished rangeSource
Yearly maintenance, small pool (up to 10,000 gallons), Phoenix$1,000 to $1,500 a yearAngi, Phoenix
Yearly maintenance, medium pool (10,000 to 20,000 gallons), Phoenix$1,500 to $2,400 a yearAngi, Phoenix
Yearly maintenance, large pool (over 20,000 gallons), Phoenix$2,400 to $3,800 a yearAngi, Phoenix
Weekly or every-other-week service$80 to $150 a monthHomeGuide, national
Pool service labor$50 to $85 an hourAngi, Phoenix
Clarifiers, scale inhibitors and acid washingAbout $15 to $40 a month on topAngi, Phoenix
Extra cleaning and filter care in monsoon monthsAbout $75 to $200 more in peak monthsAngi, Phoenix
First cleaning for a new customer$150 to $350HomeGuide, national
One-time cleaning$200 to $400HomeGuide, national
Green pool cleanup, first visit$300 to $500HomeGuide, national

Angi's Phoenix page also gives a typical figure of about $238, inside a range of $100 to $376, for pool maintenance in the city, depending on pool size, type and how often it is serviced. The page does not make plain whether that figure is per visit or per month, so treat it as a rough marker rather than a monthly price. It suggests budgeting $200 to $800 a year for extra parts and repairs, because equipment works hard in the heat. For owners who would rather do the work, Angi estimates $60 to $120 a month for chemicals, testing supplies and equipment.

The line sets no prices. Every range in the table belongs to the publisher named beside it. Your pool may come in above or below those ranges once a company has looked at it, and that company's written quote is the figure to rely on.

What moves a Phoenix pool service price up or down

Two pools on the same street can get very different quotes. These are the things a company looks at before it names a price.

Factors that raise or lower the price of pool service in the Phoenix area
FactorTends to raise the priceTends to lower the price
Pool sizeLarge pools, attached spas, water featuresSmall, simple pools
Visit frequencyWeekly visits through summer, extra storm visitsA lighter winter schedule, if the company offers one
Who supplies chemicalsRoutine chemicals built into the price, or heavy chemical useChemicals billed only as used, on a well-balanced pool
Debris loadTrees over the water, no screening, open desert or construction nearbyLittle landscaping near the pool, a block wall that cuts wind
Pets and swimmersDogs that swim, heavy daily useLight use
Equipment ageOld pumps and filters that need more attentionNewer, well-sized equipment
Salt systemCell checks and cleaning added to the visitFewer chlorine purchases over time
Hard waterScale treatment, tile cleaning, more frequent filter careWater kept in balance week after week
Starting conditionA green or neglected pool needs a cleanup firstA pool already clear and balanced

Hard water is a real factor here. The City of Phoenix's 2025 water quality report lists tap water hardness of 172 to 302 parts per million. As pools lose water to evaporation and are topped off, those minerals build up, which is one reason local companies add scale treatment.

Monthly pool service cost vs one-time cleanups

Recurring service spreads the work out. A company that sees the pool every week knows its habits, catches small changes early and keeps chemistry steady, so each visit is a known amount of work. That predictability is part of what you pay for.

One-time cleanups cost more per visit because the company is starting from an unknown condition. HomeGuide's 2026 guide puts a one-time cleaning at $200 to $400, and a green pool's first cleanup at $300 to $500 before ongoing service. A pool left green for weeks may need several visits, filter cleaning and plenty of chemicals before it is clear again.

If the pool is green now, start with the green pool cleanup page, then compare monthly plans once the water is clear.

A green pool is also a safety concern. The bottom cannot be seen, which makes it a drowning hazard, so keep children away until it is clear.

Pool repair cost: published ranges

Repairs are billed separately from service. A good service technician may spot a problem, but the repair itself is quoted on its own. Angi's 2026 national repair guides give these ranges:

Published pool repair cost ranges from Angi, 2026
RepairPublished rangeSource
Pool repairs overallAverage $725; most pay $243 to $1,212Angi, national
Pool pump repair$100 to $700Angi, national
Pool pump replacementAverage $1,300; most pay $700 to $4,000Angi, national
Pool heater repair$166 to $803; average about $479Angi, national
Leak detection$100 to $500Angi, national
Pool resurfacing, PhoenixAverage about $11,363; most pay $6,198 to $15,495Angi, Phoenix

The spread is wide because the symptom does not tell you the cause. A pump that will not run might need a small part or a whole new motor. For more on each, see the pool repair page, the pool pump repair page and the pool heater repair page. If the plaster is the question, the repair or resurface guide walks through the choice.

Check the license first. Arizona's Registrar of Contractors (ROC) licenses contractors, and its residential classifications include R-6, Swimming Pool Service and Repair. Repairs, equipment replacement and resurfacing generally call for a licensed contractor; whether a cleaning-only service needs a license is not spelled out, so ask the ROC if it matters to you. Ask the company for its ROC license number and look it up on the ROC contractor search (opens in a new tab) before work begins. The line does not check this for you.

How to compare pool service quotes

The quote with the smallest number is not always the smallest bill over a year. Put quotes side by side on the same terms:

  • Same billing period. Convert everything to a monthly or yearly figure. Some quotes are per visit, some per month.
  • Same tasks. Does each visit include brushing, vacuuming and both baskets, or only a chemical check?
  • Chemicals. Which are in the price, which are extra and how will you see what was used?
  • Filter cleaning. How often, and is it included or billed separately?
  • Storms and extras. What happens after a dust storm, and what does an extra visit cost?
  • Repairs. Are repairs always quoted in writing before work starts? Does the company hold an Arizona ROC license for repair work?
  • Terms. How much notice to cancel, and is there a contract length?

For the questions that matter when you pick a company, see the guide to choosing a pool company. For what a service plan should include, see pool service in Phoenix.

How much is pool maintenance in Arizona over a year?

The service bill is only part of owning a pool here. HomeGuide puts total yearly upkeep, including service, chemicals, electricity, water and repairs, at about $3,000 to $6,000. Water is part of it: the Arizona Department of Water Resources estimates a standard uncovered pool loses four to six feet of water a year to evaporation, and says a pool cover can save 90 to 95 percent of that loss. Budgeting for the full picture makes the monthly service price easier to judge.

Common questions

How much is pool service per month in Phoenix?

Published estimates vary. Angi's 2026 Phoenix guide puts yearly maintenance at about $1,000 to $1,500 for a small pool, $1,500 to $2,400 for a medium pool and $2,400 to $3,800 for a pool over 20,000 gallons, Dividing those yearly figures by 12 gives roughly $83 to $317 a month; that is simple arithmetic, not a monthly figure Angi publishes. HomeGuide's national figure for weekly or every-other-week service is $80 to $150 a month. Real quotes vary with the pool and what is included, and the line does not set prices.

How much does it cost to get my pool cleaned one time?

HomeGuide's 2026 guide lists a one-time cleaning at about $200 to $400, depending on pool size and the type of cleaning, and a first-time cleaning for a new customer at $150 to $350. Bringing a green, neglected pool back costs more: HomeGuide estimates $300 to $500 for the initial cleanup. The company that sees your pool gives the only price that counts.

How much does pool repair cost?

Angi's 2026 national pool repair guide gives an average of $725, with most homeowners paying $243 to $1,212. Individual repairs swing widely: Angi lists pump repairs at $100 to $700, pool heater repairs at $166 to $803 and leak detection at $100 to $500. Replacement of a whole pump or heater costs more.

Does the monthly price include chemicals?

It depends on the company. Some include routine chemicals in the service price, others bill them separately, and many charge extra for items such as stabilizer or scale treatment. Angi's Phoenix guide notes that clarifiers, scale inhibitors and acid washing can add about $15 to $40 a month. Ask for a written list of what the price covers.

Is it worth having a pool in Arizona?

That is a personal choice, but go in knowing the running costs. HomeGuide puts total yearly upkeep, including service, chemicals, electricity, water and repairs, at about $3,000 to $6,000. In the Valley, a pool can be used for much of the year, and the heat makes it a real comfort, but it also means steady care, refill water lost to evaporation and equipment that works hard in summer.
